failure_summary: All 3 runs mis-own or mis-name c1r5: the render puts it under the opponent half (opponentPunishment.entryCell + tie.sharedCells, both un-glossed in the prompt Reading key) while the only handle for it is you-immediate "(you)", and requiredSet additionally makes the opponentPunishment half be represented by handle you-major (spec c2r6, role "a single square completing YOUR four-in-a-row line") even though c2r6 is where the OPPONENT completes row 6 (c2r6·c3r6·c4r6·c5r6, all O on opponentPunishment.finalMovestring) — no opponent-owned single-square handle for c2r6 is offered at all.
notes: 3 runs in this file, not 5 (n_runs=3). Sub-sampling per rubric: A3/A4/G2/G4/G5 graded on runs 0-1 only; run 2 null for those. A1/A2/A6 copied verbatim from grade_mechanical.mjs. | A3 run0: names c2r6 as YOUR square that "wins on the spot"; board shows c2r6 is a non-gravity X major (col2 height 3) and the real lost resource is the fork completing at c2r5, pliesToEnd 8 — tactic named is not the decisive one. | A4 run0: three falsehoods — "wins on the spot" (better move lands at c2r4, win is 8 plies deep); [zone:c1r5] called "the column 2 upper square" (c1r5 is column 1); "let your opponent grab [c1r5] ... where they finish their own four-in-a-row line" (opponent completes at c2r6; visualize_board on the afterPlayed movestring 4222425326433430153304516651020 shows col1 row5 as an X [GT] major, i.e. YOUR square). | A4 run1: "the move you played leaves an immediate threat at [zone:c1r5] ... for your opponent" — the prompt states verbatim "- immediate at c1r5 (you)"; ownership inverted. | A7b run0: "the column 2 upper square" highlights a column-1 square, so the promised referent does not resolve. | A7b run2: same column-1/column-2 mismatch, plus "their central line takes over" is specific-sounding and points at nothing (opp-key-line was offered and unused). | A7c not charged on any run: no *-fork-pivot handle exists in render_decision.zones.aliases. | G1 all 3: contradict the rendered artifact — run0 inverts the L6 frame ("forced win via the lower square in column 2 ... opponent ... via the upper square in column 2"), runs 1-2 contradict the prompt Decision block ("Played move: column 1 (lands at c1r4)") and/or the afterPlayed tactic line "immediate at c1r5 (you)". | G2 runs 0-1: guardrail "name both lines with their horizons" not honored — run0 gives the wrong horizon ("on the spot" for an 8-ply forced line), run1 names the opponent line with no horizon and no location. | G4 run0: c1r5 is asserted to be where the opponent finishes four; on render_decision.finalMovestring 422242532643343015330451665102146556600 c1r5 is X 39 (your line) and X is gravity-top major at c2r5. | G7 runs 0 and 2: [zone:c1r5] wraps a phrase naming column 2, contradicting its role "the single square where you can make four next move"; annotationRepairs empty on all runs, guardDiagnostics failures empty. | Required-set omission NOT charged: run0 omits you-future-fork, runs 1-2 omit you-major, but mechanismExplainer.mjs:86/235 (missingRequiredGroups) retries in production and this harness calls the model once (OI-183) — an eval artifact, not a case failure. | G5 pass but reported: the afterPlayed threat list carries "double at c1r5 (you, window c1r5·c2r6)" — both cells are real X majors, yet c2r6 needs 3 more discs and the position is a forced loss, so the glossary sense ("your opponent cannot block both") does not hold. | Production-fidelity caveat: model is gpt-5.4-mini (what production ships), so the residual c1r5→"column 2" naming error cannot be separated from model capability; counterexamples.field_or_glossary: render_decision.requiredSet[1] = {half:"opponentPunishment", spec:"c2r6", handle:"you-major", role:"a single square completing your four-in-a-row line"}
counterexamples.evidence: c2r6 is where the OPPONENT completes four (opponentPunishment.window c2r6,c3r6,c4r6,c5r6; on opponentPunishment.finalMovestring 4222425326433430153304516651020014066611 those four cells are O 40/O 30/O 20/O 34). The render offers no opponent-owned single-square handle for it, so the required opponent half can only be pointed at with a handle whose role says the square is yours — run 0 duly wrote "the column 2 finishing square for YOUR four-in-a-row line".

counterexamples.field_or_glossary: opponentPunishment.entryCell = "c1r5" and opponentPunishment.tie.sharedCells = ["c1r5"] — both printed in the prompt evidence JSON with no entry in the "# Reading key" section
counterexamples.evidence: c1r5 is YOUR gravity-top major on the afterPlayed board (visualize_board 4222425326433430153304516651020: "Major threats: col1 row5 (X) [GT]"), and the prompt says so verbatim ("- immediate at c1r5 (you)"). The opponent only BLOCKS there. Listing the same cell under the opponent half without a gloss is the only prompt-side signal supporting runs 0 and 1 handing c1r5 to the opponent.

counterexamples.field_or_glossary: zone alias "you-immediate" (spec c1r5) is the sole handle for c1r5; no handle expresses "the square your opponent must take away from you"
counterexamples.evidence: The real teaching point of this blunder — column 1 forces the opponent to occupy c1r5, the very square your winning row-5 line (lostResource.window c1r5,c2r5,c3r5,c4r5) needs — has no offered handle, so no run states it; all three instead reach for a wrong-owner or wrong-column paraphrase.
